Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

questions.solution:

• The word **"Misanthrope"** refers to a person who dislikes humankind and avoids human society. (मानवजाति से घृणा करने वाला)
 
 
• **Example:** After years of betrayal, he became a misanthrope, preferring solitude over social gatherings.
 
 
• The word **"Disdain"** in the question aligns with the qualities of a misanthrope, as disdain means a feeling of contempt or scorn for others. (अवमानना)
 
 
• **Example:** Ravi's disdain for humanity was evident in the way he isolated himself from society.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Misanthrope**.

• **Example:** His misogynist views were evident in his discriminatory remarks about women in leadership roles.
 
 
 
• **Cynic** (निंदक): A person who believes people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable reasons.
 
 
• **Example:** As a cynic, he never trusted anyone's intentions, always assuming they had selfish motives.
 
 
 
• **Narcissist** (आत्ममोहित व्यक्ति): A person who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves.

questions.question:
Identify Spot the error in the given sentence.

"Neither of the two boys have completed his homework."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in the phrase "**boys have**."
 
• When a sentence begins with "**Neither of**," "**Either of**," or "**Each of**," the subject is considered **singular** because it refers to the individuals one at a time.
 
• According to the rules of **Subject-Verb Agreement**, a singular subject must be followed by a **singular verb**.
 
• Therefore, the plural verb "**have**" should be replaced with the singular verb "**has**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Neither of the two boys **has** completed his homework."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Singular Pronouns:** Since "Neither" is singular, the possessive pronoun that follows must also be singular. In this sentence, "**his**" is already correctly used, reinforcing that the verb should also be singular.
 
• **Option 1 & 4:** These parts are grammatically correct. "Neither of the two" correctly sets up the choice between two individuals.
 
• **Distinction:** Don't be confused by the plural noun "boys." While the noun following "of" is plural, the **real subject** is "Neither," which is singular.

questions.question:
Identify Spot the error in the given sentence.

"Neither the captain nor the players has arrived yet."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in the phrase "**has arrived**."
 
• When two subjects are joined by "**Neither... nor**" or "**Either... or**," the verb must agree with the **subject nearest to it**. This is known as the **Rule of Proximity**.
 
• In this sentence, there are two subjects: "**the captain**" (singular) and "**the players**" (plural).
 
• Since the plural subject "**the players**" is closer to the verb, the verb must also be plural. Therefore, "**has**" should be replaced with "**have**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Neither the captain nor the players **have** arrived yet."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule of Proximity:** If the subjects were reversed ("Neither the players nor the **captain**"), the singular verb "**has**" would then be correct because "captain" would be the closest subject.
 
• **Distinction:** Do not confuse this with "Neither of..." (from the previous question), which always takes a singular verb because "Neither" acts as the lone singular subject. In "Neither... nor," there are two distinct subjects to consider.
 
• **Option 4: "yet"** – This is an adverb correctly used in a negative sentence to indicate an expected action has not happened.

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The child said, "I am ten years old."

options.text: The child said that he has been ten years old.
The child said that he had been ten years old.
The child said that he was ten years old.
The child said that he is ten years old.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reporting Verb:** The reporting verb **"said"** remains **"said"** in the indirect speech as there is no listener mentioned to change it to "told."
 
• **Conjunction:** The comma and inverted commas are removed, and the conjunction **"that"** is used to introduce the reported clause.
 
• **Pronoun Change:** The first-person pronoun **"I"** (referring to the child) changes to the third-person **"he"** (or "she," but "he" is the standard convention in these options).
 
• **Tense Change:** When the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the **Simple Present** tense (**"am"**) in direct speech changes to the **Simple Past** tense (**"was"**) in indirect speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The child said that he was ten years old."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses **"has been"** (Present Perfect), which is the wrong tense shift for a simple present statement.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses **"had been"** (Past Perfect), which would only be correct if the direct speech was in the Simple Past ("I was ten").
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it retains the **Present Simple** ("is"), which is only acceptable if the statement is a universal truth or if the situation is still exactly the same at the moment of reporting (though standard grammar rules require the backshift to "was").

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

It is being claimed that a new species has been discovered in the Amazon.

options.text: Someone is claiming that a new species has been discovered in the Amazon.
A new species has been discovered in the Amazon, it is being claimed.
Someone claims that a new species has been discovered in the Amazon.
Someone is claiming that they have discovered a new species in the Amazon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** using the **Present Continuous** tense ("is being claimed").
 
• When a sentence starts with "It is being [verb-ed]," it is an impersonal passive. To change it to **Active Voice**, we introduce an indefinite subject like **"Someone"** or **"They."**
 
• **Match the Tense:** The passive form "is being claimed" (Present Continuous Passive) must be converted to "is claiming" (Present Continuous Active).
 
• The clause following "that" ("a new species has been discovered...") is a separate passive construction that provides the content of the claim. In Option 1, this clause remains consistent with the original statement's focus.
 
• The structure becomes: *Subject (Someone) + is claiming + that + [the rest of the information].*

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Someone is claiming that a new species has been discovered in the Amazon."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"A new species has been discovered..., it is being claimed." – This is simply a rearrangement of the passive voice, not a conversion to active form.
 
• **Option 3: **"Someone claims..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense from **Present Continuous** to **Simple Present**.
 
• **Option 4: **"Someone is claiming that they have discovered..." – This unnecessarily changes the second part of the sentence ("a new species has been discovered") into active voice, which might not be accurate if the "someone" claiming it isn't the one who discovered it.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

What are they building?

options.text: What has been built by them?
What is being built by them?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence "What are they building?" is an **Interrogative sentence** in the **Present Continuous Tense**.
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The active form uses *is/am/are + verb-ing*. The passive form for this tense requires **is/am/are + being + V3 (past participle)**.
 
• **Structure for Interrogative Passive:** *Question word (What) + is/are + being + V3 + by + agent.*
 
• Since "What" acts as the object being asked about (and is treated as singular here), we use **"is being built."**
 
• The subject "they" changes to the object **"them"** after the preposition "by."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"What is being built by them?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"What has been built..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to **Present Perfect**.
 
• **Option 3: **"What was built..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to **Simple Past**.
 
• **Option 4: **"What were they building?" – Incorrect because it is still in the **Active Voice** (Past Continuous) and merely changes the tense.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The historian concluded that the ancient civilization had developed advanced irrigation techniques long before its demise.

options.text: The historian said, "The ancient civilization had developed advanced irrigation techniques long before its demise."
The historian said, "The ancient civilization developed advanced irrigation techniques long before its demise."
The historian concluded, "The ancient civilization develops advanced irrigation techniques."
The historian said, "The ancient civilization has developed advanced irrigation techniques."

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The historian concluded that the ancient civilization had developed advanced irrigation techniques long before its demise.
 
• **Tense Change (Indirect to Direct):** In indirect speech, the **Past Perfect** tense ("had developed") is used to report an action that was already in the **Simple Past** ("developed") in the original direct speech. When converting back to direct voice, we shift the tense forward.
 
• **Reporting Verb:** The reporting verb **"concluded"** in indirect speech can be represented by **"said"** in direct speech while maintaining the core meaning.
 
• **Conjunction:** The conjunction **"that"** is removed, and the original statement is placed within quotation marks.
 
• **Context:** Since the historian is talking about a completed historical event, the **Simple Past** ("developed") is the most natural and grammatically correct form for the original statement.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The historian said, 'The ancient civilization developed advanced irrigation techniques long before its demise.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it retains **"had developed"** (Past Perfect). While technically possible for very specific sequences of past events, "had developed" in indirect speech is almost always a backshifted "developed" (Simple Past) from the direct version.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it uses **"develops"** (Simple Present), which suggests a habitual action or a current state, which does not fit a historical demise.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses **"has developed"** (Present Perfect), which implies a connection to the present that is inconsistent with a civilization that has already met its demise.

questions.question:
In the sentence:

"While remote work offers flexibility and saves commuting time, many experts argue that working from the office remains more effective for several reasons."

What is the part of speech of the word "flexibility"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4** i.e '**Noun**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"flexibility"** is a **noun** because it refers to a quality or a state of being, specifically the ability to be easily modified.
 
• In the sentence, "flexibility" acts as the **direct object** of the verb "offers," answering the question of what remote work provides.
 
• The suffix **"-ity"** is a common indicator of a noun in English (e.g., activity, purity, responsibility).
 
• Nouns typically follow verbs like "offer," "provide," or "give" when those verbs are used to describe features or benefits.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective: **The adjective form is **"flexible,"** which would be used to describe a noun (e.g., "a flexible schedule"). 
 
• **Adverb**: The adverb form is **"flexibly,"** which would modify a verb or adjective (e.g., "to work flexibly").
 
• **Verb:** While **"flex"** is a related verb, "flexibility" itself cannot express an action; it only names the quality.

questions.question:
In the sentence:

"Another important factor is the psychological impact."

What type of adjective is the word "psychological"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Descriptive adjective**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"psychological"** is a **descriptive adjective** because it describes the nature or kind of the noun "impact."
 
• **Descriptive adjectives** (also known as qualitative adjectives) add a quality or characteristic to the noun they modify, answering the question "What kind?"
 
• In this context, it specifies that the impact is related to the mind or mental state, rather than being a physical or financial impact.
 
• The suffix **"-ical"** is a common ending for adjectives derived from nouns (e.g., biology to biological, psychology to psychological).

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

questions.question: A rectangular garden has a length of 20 meters and a width of 15 meters. If a path of 2 meters wide is built around it (outside the garden), what is the area of the path?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: The area of the path = Area of the larger rectangle (garden + path) − Area of the garden.

Calculation:

Length of larger rectangle = 20 + 2 + 2 = 24 meters

Width of larger rectangle = 15 + 2 + 2 = 19 meters

Area of larger rectangle = 24 × 19 = 456 sq m

Area of garden = 20 × 15 = 300 sq m

Area of path = 456 − 300 = 156 sq m

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

questions.question: Which of the following titles means "Lord of the three worlds"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tribhuvana-chakravartin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tribhuvana-chakravartin** is a Sanskrit term that translates to "Lord of the Three Worlds." It signifies a ruler whose dominion encompasses the entire earth, heaven, and the underworld.
 
• This title was historically used by Indian monarchs to denote their supreme sovereignty and universal rule over these realms, symbolizing both spiritual and political authority.
 
• The concept of "Three Worlds" is rooted in ancient Indian cosmology, where the world is divided into three planes of existence: **earth (prithvi), heaven (swarga), and the underworld (patala).**
 
• The title "Tribhuvana-chakravartin" was often claimed by emperors during the **Gupta Empire** and other prominent dynasties to assert their supremacy as universal rulers.
 
• This title also carried immense religious significance, aligning with Hindu beliefs of cosmic order and the ruler's role as the protector of dharma (universal law).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maharaja-adhiraja:**

 
 
• This title translates to "Great King of Kings" and was used to denote supreme rulers in ancient India.
 
• It emphasized the ruler's authority over subordinate kings and vassals rather than universal dominion.
 
• For example, rulers of the **Gupta Empire** and other dynasties often adopted this title to assert their political dominance.
 
 
 
• **Ekrat-Samrat:**
 
 
• "Ekrat" means "sole ruler," and "Samrat" refers to "emperor." Together, this title indicates an unchallenged ruler of a specific region or empire.
 
• It was used by Indian kings to signify their absolute authority within their territories.
 
• This title does not imply control over the "Three Worlds" and is more regionally confined.
 
 
 
• **Devraja:**
 
 
• "Devraja" translates to "King of Gods" and primarily refers to the divine status of the ruler.
 
• This title was closely linked to the notion of divine kingship, where the monarch was considered an earthly representative of the gods.
 
• It was prominently used in Southeast Asia, especially in kingdoms like the Khmer Empire.
 
 
 
• **Tribhuvana-chakravartin:**
 
 
• This title signifies universal sovereignty and is deeply rooted in Indian cosmological and spiritual traditions.
 
• It encompasses control over the three realms: **earth, heaven, and the underworld**, symbolizing both spiritual and political supremacy.
 
• It was widely used during the reigns of powerful dynasties such as the **Cholas, Guptas, and Mauryas** to reflect their aspirations of global and cosmic rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Usage:**

 
 
• The title "Tribhuvana-chakravartin" was not merely political; it had religious significance as rulers were seen as upholders of dharma.
 
• It was used by emperors like **Samudragupta** and **Rajaraja Chola** to assert their universal rule and divine favor.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Context:**
 
 
• The idea of "Three Worlds" aligns with Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain cosmology, emphasizing the interconnectedness of earthly, divine, and spiritual realms.
 
• Rulers adopting this title were often portrayed in inscriptions and art as supreme protectors and benefactors of their subjects.

__
 
• The **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**, 2016, introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (G.S.T.)**, marking a significant reform in India’s tax system.
 
• The Act paved the way for the creation of a **unified indirect tax regime** by subsuming multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, VAT, and others into a single tax structure.
 
• The amendment added **Articles 246A, 269A, and 279A** to the Constitution, granting the central and state governments the concurrent power to legislate on GST.
 
• The **GST Council**, established under **Article 279A**, was given the authority to recommend rates, exemptions, and other related policies for the smooth implementation of GST.
 
• The **President of India** gave his assent to the bill on **8th September 2016**, following its passage by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• GST was officially launched on **1st July 2017**, replacing the complex indirect tax structure and fostering ease of doing business across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST):**

 
 
• GST is a **destination-based consumption tax**, meaning the tax revenue accrues to the state where the goods or services are consumed.
 
• It is implemented in four tax slabs: **5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%**, with certain essential items being exempted.
 
• GST is divided into three types: **CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST)**, ensuring revenue distribution between the central and state governments.
 
• This tax reform aimed to eliminate the cascading effect of taxes, thereby reducing the overall tax burden on consumers.
 
• India adopted a **dual GST model**, which is unique compared to other countries implementing GST.
 
 
 
• **Articles Introduced by the 101st Amendment:**
 
 
• **Article 246A:** Grants the central and state governments **simultaneous powers** to legislate on GST.
 
• **Article 269A:** Specifies the levy and collection of GST on **inter-state transactions** by the central government, with revenue shared between the center and states.
 
• **Article 279A:** Establishes the **GST Council**, comprising the Union Finance Minister and state finance ministers, to recommend GST policies.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• Comprises the Union Finance Minister (Chairperson), Union Minister of State for Finance, and representatives from all state governments.
 
• Decides on critical matters such as tax rates, exemptions, registration procedures, and dispute resolution mechanisms.
 
• Ensures **harmonized tax practices** across states to promote uniformity and simplicity.
 
 
 
• **Impact of GST:**
 
 
• Encouraged **formalization** of businesses and improved tax compliance.
 
• Reduced the overall **tax burden** by eliminating overlapping taxes and simplifying the tax structure.
 
• Boosted **economic growth** by fostering ease of doing business and attracting foreign investments.
 
• Ensured seamless movement of goods across state borders by eliminating **check-post delays**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Previous Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• **100th Amendment Act:** Ratified the **India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement** in 2015.
 
• **102nd Amendment Act:** Granted constitutional status to the **National Commission for Backward Classes** in 2018.
 
• **103rd Amendment Act:** Introduced **10% reservation** for economically weaker sections (EWS) in 2019.
 
 
 
• **GST in Other Countries:**
 
 
• First introduced in **France in 1954**, GST has been adopted by over **160 countries** worldwide.
 
• Countries like **Canada** and **Australia** follow a dual GST model similar to India.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in GST Implementation:**
 
 
• Initial **technical glitches** in the GST portal hindered smooth compliance.
 
• Complexity in **classification** of goods and services under different tax slabs.
 
• Delay in **refund processing** for exporters created cash flow issues.

__
 
• **Integration of TB services within the public health system** is a crucial step for ensuring **equitable and universal health coverage**, as it allows for accessible and affordable treatment for tuberculosis patients, particularly in underserved areas. *Statement II is correct.*
 
• **Equitable and universal health coverage** is one of the goals of the Indian government under the **Ayushman Bharat Program** and other health initiatives, aiming to provide comprehensive healthcare services to all citizens irrespective of their socioeconomic status.
 
• Statement I, concerning the **eradication of malaria**, is unrelated to the integration of TB services. Malaria eradication requires separate strategies such as vector control, distribution of insecticide-treated nets, and antimalarial drugs. *Hence, Statement I is incorrect.*
 
• The integration of TB services ensures that TB patients receive timely diagnosis, free-of-cost treatment, and follow-up care through the public health system. This contributes to reducing the disease burden and aligns with the goal of achieving universal health coverage.
 
• The World Health Organization (**WHO**) has recognized the importance of integrating TB services into public health systems to meet global targets for TB elimination by **2030** under the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):**

 
 
• **TB** is caused by the bacterium **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** and primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.
 
• India has the highest burden of TB cases globally, accounting for nearly **26%** of the world's TB cases as per the **Global TB Report 2022**.
 
• The Government of India aims to eliminate TB by **2025**, five years ahead of the global SDG target of **2030**.
 
 
 
• **National Tuberculosis Elimination Program (NTEP):**
 
 
• Formerly known as the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Program (RNTCP), it was renamed in 2020 to reflect the goal of eliminating TB in India.
 
• The program focuses on early diagnosis, free treatment, and reducing stigma associated with TB through awareness campaigns.
 
• It also includes innovations such as **Nikshay Poshan Yojana**, which provides **nutritional support of Rs. 500 per month** to TB patients.
 
 
 
• **Universal Health Coverage (UHC):**
 
 
• UHC ensures that all individuals and communities have access to essential health services without financial hardship.
 
• It is a core component of the **World Health Organization's (WHO)** Global Health Strategy and is part of the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3.8).**
 
• India's UHC efforts include programs like **Ayushman Bharat**, which provides health insurance coverage of **Rs. 5 lakh per family per year** for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
 
 
• **Malaria Eradication:**
 
 
• Malaria eradication involves strategies like the distribution of **insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs)**, indoor residual spraying (IRS), and the use of antimalarial drugs.
 
• India aims to eliminate malaria by **2030**, as part of the **National Framework for Malaria Elimination (NFME) 2016-2030.**
 
• While TB and malaria are both significant public health challenges, their eradication strategies are different and require separate interventions.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDG 3** focuses on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all at all ages.
 
• Under this goal, the target is to **end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria**, and neglected tropical diseases by **2030**.
 
• India's efforts to integrate TB services into the public health system are aligned with achieving this target.

questions.question: In which year did Tipu Sultan become the ruler of Mysore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1782**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tipu Sultan**, also known as the "Tiger of Mysore," became the ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore in the year **1782**.
 
• Tipu Sultan succeeded his father, **Hyder Ali**, after his death during the **Second Anglo-Mysore War** in the same year.
 
• He was known for his exceptional military skills, administrative reforms, and efforts to modernize his army.
 
• Tipu Sultan ruled Mysore until his death in **1799** during the **Fourth Anglo-Mysore War**, where he was killed in the siege of Srirangapatna.
 
• Tipu Sultan is celebrated for his resistance against British colonial expansion and his innovative measures in governance, including introducing new coinage and promoting trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hyder Ali’s Role:**

 
 
• Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan’s father, was the founder of the **Kingdom of Mysore** and played a crucial role in establishing a strong military and administrative foundation.
 
• He was a key figure in the First and Second Anglo-Mysore Wars against the British East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Anglo-Mysore Wars:**
 
 
• Tipu Sultan actively participated in the **Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–1784)** alongside his father, Hyder Ali.
 
• He continued the struggle against the British in the **Third (1790–1792)** and **Fourth Anglo-Mysore Wars (1798–1799)**.
 
 
 
• **Tipu Sultan’s Reforms:**
 
 
• He introduced several administrative reforms, including a new system of taxation and revenue collection.
 
• He promoted agriculture, trade, and industry, and is credited with introducing the cultivation of **silk in Mysore**, which remains a hallmark of the region.
 
 
 
• **Military Innovations:**
 
 
• Tipu Sultan is renowned for his use of **rocketry in warfare**, particularly the Mysorean rockets, which were an early precursor to modern military technology.
 
• He also sought alliances with foreign powers, including the **French**, to counter British dominance.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Tipu Sultan is remembered as a valiant warrior and a symbol of resistance against colonial rule.
 
• His innovations and efforts to modernize Mysore have left a lasting impact on the region’s history and development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tipu Sultan’s Treaty:**

 
 
• The **Treaty of Mangalore (1784)** was signed between Tipu Sultan and the British after the Second Anglo-Mysore War, restoring territories to both sides.
 
 
 
• **Death of Tipu Sultan:**
 
 
• Tipu Sultan was killed on **4 May 1799** during the siege of Srirangapatna, marking the end of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
 
• His death symbolized the collapse of Mysore's resistance to British expansion in South India.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Indian History:**
 
 
• Tipu Sultan’s resistance against the British inspired later freedom fighters in India’s struggle for independence.
 
• His legacy is celebrated in Indian history as a pioneer of anti-colonial resistance.

questions.question: What is the first hour of Lok Sabha proceedings called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Question hour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Question Hour** is the first hour of a sitting session in the Lok Sabha, which is dedicated to questions by the Members of Parliament (MPs) to ministers in order to hold the government accountable.
 
• It is a parliamentary mechanism in India, conducted every day during the sessions of both Houses of Parliament, i.e., Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• During **Question Hour**, MPs ask questions that may be related to legislative, administrative, or policy issues, and ministers are obliged to provide accurate and precise answers.
 
• Questions can be categorized into three types: **Starred Questions** (answered orally), **Unstarred Questions** (answered in written form), and **Short Notice Questions** (asked with shorter notice than the usual 10 days).
 
• **Question Hour** serves as a key tool for parliamentary oversight, ensuring transparency and accountability in governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero Hour:**

 
 
• **Zero Hour** starts immediately after Question Hour and lasts until the agenda for the session is taken up.
 
• Unlike Question Hour, Zero Hour is not officially mentioned in parliamentary rules but has become a convention in parliamentary proceedings.
 
• During Zero Hour, MPs can raise urgent issues without prior notice, and ministers may or may not respond immediately.
 
 
 
• **Public Hour:**
 
 
• This term is not officially recognized as part of Lok Sabha proceedings. It may be incorrectly used to refer to any other parliamentary session where public issues are discussed.
 
 
 
• **Privilege Hour:**
 
 
• This is not a formal term used in Indian parliamentary proceedings. However, privilege motions can be raised when a member feels a breach of privilege has occurred.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Question Hour:**
 
 
• It provides an opportunity for MPs to scrutinize the functioning of the government and seek accountability for its policies and actions.
 
• It ensures that the executive remains answerable to the legislature and indirectly to the citizens.
 
• It enables MPs to highlight specific issues affecting their constituencies and seek remedies from the concerned ministries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timings of Question Hour:**

 
 
• In Lok Sabha, Question Hour is typically held from **11:00 AM to 12:00 PM**.
 
• In Rajya Sabha, it is conducted from **11:00 AM to 12:00 PM**, though the timings can vary depending on parliamentary sessions.
 
 
 
• **Types of Questions:**
 
 
• **Starred Questions:** These require oral answers and allow supplementary questions to be asked.
 
• **Unstarred Questions:** These require written answers and do not allow supplementary questions.
 
• **Short Notice Questions:** These pertain to urgent matters and require a shorter notice period than usual.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The practice of **Question Hour** began during the colonial period, continuing to serve as a vital mechanism in parliamentary democracy.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Pandemic Impact:**
 
 
• In 2020, Question Hour was temporarily suspended during the Monsoon Session of Parliament due to the COVID-19 pandemic, raising concerns about reduced accountability.

questions.question: According to the Census 2011, which state had a negative growth rate in decadal population?

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011**, **Nagaland** recorded a **negative decadal growth rate** in population, with a decline of **-0.58%**.
 
• This negative growth rate is attributed to factors such as **out-migration**, inaccuracies in previous census data, and better enumeration practices during the **Census 2011**.
 
• It was the only state in India to show a **negative decadal growth rate** during the period 2001-2011.
 
• The population of Nagaland, as per Census 2011, was **1,978,502**, which was a decrease from the 2001 Census population of **1,990,036**.
 
• This phenomenon highlights the unique demographic challenges in certain regions of India, particularly in the **Northeast**, which may include migration patterns and socio-economic factors.

__
 
• **Decadal Population Growth:**

 
 
• Decadal growth refers to the percentage increase or decrease in population during a 10-year period, as recorded by the **Census of India**.
 
• It is an important indicator of demographic trends, influencing policy-making, resource allocation, and regional development planning.
 
 
 
• **Nagaland's Demographic Features:**

• The state is known for its tribal culture and hilly terrain, which contribute to its unique demographic and socio-economic dynamics.
 
• Out-migration to other states for education, jobs, and better living conditions is a significant factor in its population trends.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011 Highlights:**

• The state with the highest population growth rate was **Meghalaya**, while Nagaland recorded the lowest growth rate.

• States in the northeastern region often face unique challenges, such as difficult terrain, inadequate infrastructure, and socio-political issues, which impact population growth.
 
• Migration to metropolitan areas like Delhi, Bengaluru, and Mumbai for better opportunities is a common trend.
 
 
 
• **Implications of Negative Growth:**
 
 
• A declining population can lead to challenges such as reduced workforce, economic stagnation, and pressure on social security systems.
 
• However, it can also ease pressure on local resources and reduce environmental degradation, depending on the context.

• **Indira Gandhi**, the then Prime Minister of India, served as the chairman of the **Planning Commission** during the **Fourth Five-Year Plan** (1969–1974).
 
• The **Planning Commission of India** was responsible for formulating India’s Five-Year Plans, which aimed to develop the nation’s economy.
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan** focused on **self-reliance** in agriculture and industrial production, addressing the challenges posed by the **India-Pakistan war in 1965** and the **1971 Bangladesh Liberation War**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a factor responsible for having different types of rural settlements in India?

I. Physical features

II. Social structure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Physical features:** The geographical and environmental factors such as **terrain, climate, and availability of water resources** play a significant role in determining the type of rural settlements. For example, settlements in hilly areas tend to be dispersed, while those in plains are more compact. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• **Social structure:** Social and cultural factors such as **caste system, community practices, and economic activities** influence the layout and organization of rural settlements. Regions with distinct cultural identities may have unique settlement patterns. *Hence, statement II is correct.*
 
• Rural settlements vary across India due to the interplay of **physical and social factors**. For instance, settlements in Kerala are linear due to the influence of physical features like backwaters and social aspects like economic activities.
 
• The classification of rural settlements in India into **compact, semi-compact, dispersed, and hamlets** reflects the impact of these factors.
 
• The combined influence of physical and social elements ensures diversity in rural settlements, making India a unique study in settlement geography.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Rural Settlements in India:**

 
 
• **Compact settlements:** Found in fertile plains and regions with abundant water resources, where houses are closely packed together. Example: Gangetic plains.
 
• **Semi-compact settlements:** Found in less fertile areas or regions with moderate resources. Houses are moderately spaced. Example: Parts of Rajasthan.
 
• **Dispersed settlements:** Found in hilly terrains, forests, or areas with difficult accessibility. Houses are scattered. Example: Himalayan regions.
 
• **Hamlets:** Small clusters of houses separated by fields, often found in tribal areas. Example: Villages in Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Physical Factors Influencing Settlements:**
 
 
• **Terrain:** Flat plains encourage compact settlements, while mountains lead to dispersed settlements.
 
• **Climate:** Cold or arid regions often have smaller, scattered settlements.
 
• **Water availability:** Close proximity to rivers or lakes leads to larger settlements.
 
 
 
• **Social Factors Influencing Settlements:**
 
 
• **Cultural practices:** Communities with shared cultural identities often cluster together.
 
• **Economic activities:** Regions with intensive agricultural or industrial activities have compact settlements.
 
• **Historical factors:** Many settlements are influenced by historical trade routes or colonial policies.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Diversity in Rural Settlements:**
 
 
• Settlements in Kerala are linear due to the influence of physical features like backwaters and social aspects like fishing and agriculture.
 
• Rural areas in Rajasthan show dispersed patterns due to arid climate and limited water resources.
 
• Himalayan regions have scattered settlements due to rugged terrain and climatic conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Settlements and their Evolution:** The rural settlement pattern in India has evolved due to the interplay of **geographical, cultural, and economic factors**. Historical influences like colonial land systems also shaped settlement types.
 
• **Regional Variations:** The diversity in settlement types reflects India's geographical and cultural variations, making it a unique study area in geography.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Policies like the **Integrated Rural Development Programme** aim to improve the living conditions in rural areas, influencing settlement patterns.

questions.question: Which metal was first used by early human communities in ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper** was the first metal used by early human communities in ancient India. It marked the beginning of the **Chalcolithic Age**, also known as the Copper Age.
 
• The use of copper began around **3000 BCE**, primarily in regions such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra in India.
 
• Early humans made tools, utensils, and ornaments from copper due to its **malleability** and ease of extraction.
 
• It was widely used before the discovery of iron or bronze, as these metals required more advanced smelting techniques.
 
• The widespread use of copper revolutionized tool-making and laid the foundation for advancements in agriculture, trade, and craftsmanship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iron:**

 
 
• Iron was used much later during the **Iron Age**, which began around **1200 BCE** in India.
 
• Its discovery required advanced smelting techniques and led to stronger tools and weapons.
 
• The widespread use of iron contributed to significant advancements in agriculture, warfare, and construction.
 
 
 
• **Bronze:**
 
 
• Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, marked the **Bronze Age**, which began around **3300 BCE** in other parts of the world.
 
• In India, the use of bronze was not as widespread as copper due to the limited availability of tin.
 
• Bronze was primarily used for crafting weapons and ceremonial items.
 
 
 
• **Gold:**
 
 
• Gold was used for ornamental purposes by ancient civilizations but was not suitable for making tools or weapons.
 
• India has a long history of gold usage, especially in religious and cultural contexts.
 
• The Harappan civilization extensively traded gold with Mesopotamia and other regions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Copper:**
 
 
• Copper's discovery and usage marked a shift from the Stone Age to the **Chalcolithic Age**, facilitating human progress.
 
• It allowed early humans to create more durable and efficient tools, enhancing productivity in agriculture and other fields.
 
• Sites such as **Rajasthan's Balathal** and **Gujarat's Lothal** have revealed evidence of copper usage in ancient India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chalcolithic Age:**

 
 
• The Chalcolithic Age refers to the transition period between the Stone Age and the Bronze Age, marked by the use of copper tools.
 
• It lasted in India from approximately **3000 BCE to 1000 BCE**.
 
• Important Chalcolithic sites in India include **Ahar**, **Kayatha**, and **Malwa**.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Findings:**
 
 
• Excavations in sites like **Rajasthan's Ganeshwar** and **Gujarat's Lothal** have uncovered copper artifacts such as tools, beads, and ornaments.
 
• These findings highlight the technological advancements and trade practices of early human communities.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Economy:**
 
 
• Copper was a valuable commodity and played a significant role in early trade networks.
 
• It was traded locally and internationally, contributing to the economic development of ancient societies.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Metallurgy:**
 
 
• The use of copper paved the way for the discovery and utilization of other metals such as bronze and iron.
 
• Metallurgy evolved significantly, leading to advancements in construction, weapon-making, and various crafts.
